docRequirement: claude-directory.md:293 (the tips array on the `commands/` node) binds bare-name precedence: "If a skill and command share a name, the skill takes precedence". The same sentence is on skills.md:122 and slash-commands.md:122 ("if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence"). So with `commands/review.md` and a skill whose name is `review` both present, exactly one `/review` must exist and it must be the SKILL.
current: The opposite, deliberately. `selectSkillSlashCommands` skips any skill whose `logicalName` is already claimed: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:444 — `if (taken.has(skill.logicalName)) continue;` — and its JSDoc states the inverted rule as the intent (custom-commands.ts:432-434: "`takenNames` wins: when an explicit command file already provides `/review`, the skill does not also claim that bare name. Explicit commands are authored for this purpose and are the more specific declaration."). Both call sites populate `takenNames` from the discovered command files: SessionManager.skillSlashCommands (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16006-16014) forwards the argument, and the listing path (SessionManager.ts:16039) and the resolution path (SessionManager.ts:16120) each pass `nativeCommands.map(command => command.name)`. `nativeCommands` is `loadSessionCustomSlashCommands` (SessionManager.ts:15837-15884): real `.nessy-agent/commands/*.md` and `.agents/commands/*.md` files via `discoverCustomSlashCommands` (aliased import at SessionManager.ts:305 of `listCustomSlashCommands`, packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:180-220, which mints `id: custom:<name>`, `label: /<name>` at :169-171) PLUS every workflow recipe name (SessionManager.ts:15873-15882). Because the skip at custom-commands.ts:444 `continue`s BEFORE the push at :447, the shadowed skill contributes no entry at all — not even a namespaced one — so `listCustomSlashCommandSummaries` returns `[...native, ...plugin, ...skills, ...mcp]` (SessionManager.ts:16044) with no `custom:skill:review`, and `resolveCustomSlashCommand`'s skill lookup at SessionManager.ts:16119-16121 cannot find that id either. The behaviour is pinned by tests: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.test.ts:172-178 asserts `selectSkillSlashCommands([skill('review'), skill('audit')], ['review'])` yields only `audit` under the comment "Precedence: an explicit command file wins", and packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/custom-slash-command-boundary.test.ts writes a real `.nessy-agent/commands/review.md` (:520-522) and asserts the summaries are exactly `['custom:review', skillSlashCommandId('deploy')]` (:593-596). The choice was made by an executor: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md left it open ("Decide the precedence between an explicit custom command and a skill-derived one, and state it in the commit body") and tracker row 5 recorded "Precedence: an explicit command file wins the bare `/name`" under commit 94cb0f9c, citing no Claude page.
divergence: The precedence direction is inverted; nothing else. The ids, labels, bodies and menu plumbing are all correct — `custom:skill:<name>` vs `custom:<name>` already keep the two addressable apart (custom-commands.ts:285-287 and :169), so this is purely which of the two colliding entries is emitted. Two secondary deltas fall out of the same line: (1) the loser is dropped entirely rather than kept under its namespaced id — the tracker's claim that the skill "keeps only its namespaced `custom:skill:<name>` id" is inaccurate, because :444 `continue`s before :447; (2) workflow-recipe names ride the same `takenNames` array (SessionManager.ts:15873-15882 feeding :16039/:16120), so a workflow also shadows a same-named skill — a surface Claude's pages say nothing about.

change.what: Keep the function's mechanics (the `taken` set still does skill-vs-skill dedup at :445) but restate the contract: `takenNames` is now only the reservations a skill may NOT take over (workflow-recipe names), not explicit command names. Rewrite the JSDoc bullet at :432-434 to quote claude-directory.md:293 and say the skill wins the bare name against a command file. No change to the loop body itself if the caller stops passing command names; if you prefer to keep the caller simple, change the signature to `selectSkillSlashCommands(skills, reservedNames)` and additionally return the set of claimed names so the caller can filter its own list.

Stop passing command-file names as taken. At :16039 pass only the workflow-derived names — `nativeCommands.filter(command => command.source === 'workflow').map(command => command.name)` — then compute the skill list FIRST and filter the native summaries with it: drop any `nativeCommands` entry whose `source !== 'workflow'` and whose `name` is in the selected skill names, before `toCustomSlashCommandSummary` at :16020. The final array at :16044 must contain exactly one entry per bare name; a duplicate `/review` is not acceptable because the renderer's typed-input matcher picks by `label` in array order (see blastRadius).

Same `takenNames` change at :16120 so the skill id now resolves. Decide explicitly whether the shadowed `custom:<name>` command file stays resolvable: today the native lookup short-circuits at :16086-16087 before any capability snapshot is resolved, and making the shadowed id fail would require resolving a snapshot on the native path (a real cost). Listing-only shadowing is enough for the documented contract; if you keep the id resolvable, say so in the commit body — the RPC accepts arbitrary ids (packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:323).

change.what: Invert it. The comment at :173-174 and the assertion at :175-177 both encode the wrong rule. Retarget the case at the new contract: a reserved workflow name still blocks, an explicit-command name no longer reaches this function.

change.symbol: 'registers a /slug per user-invocable skill, skips user-invocable: false, and lets an explicit command win' (:516-614)
change.what: Rename it and flip the expectation at :593-596: with the `.nessy-agent/commands/review.md` fixture at :520-522 and a `review` skill, summaries must be `[skillSlashCommandId('deploy'), skillSlashCommandId('review')]` with no `custom:review`, and `resolveCustomSlashCommand(session, skillSlashCommandId('review'))` must return the `[skill:review] $ARGUMENTS` body. Add one negative case: a workflow-named collision still keeps the workflow (or flip it too, if the owner decides workflows lose as well).

blastRadius: Two callers only: SessionManager.ts:16039 (listing) and :16120 (resolution), both through the private `skillSlashCommands` (:16006). Downstream of the listing: ISessionManager.listCustomSlashCommandSummaries (packages/server-core/src/handlers/session-manager-interface.ts:143) → RPC packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/workspace.ts:78 → renderer `customSlashCommands` state (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/AppShell.tsx:892, passed at :1723) → apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/FreeFormInput.tsx:365/1077 → the `/` menu (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/ui/slash-command-menu.tsx). CRITICAL detail for the fix: typed-input dispatch (apps/electron/src/renderer/components/app-shell/input/custom-slash-command-submission.ts:20-33) matches on `candidate.label` with `commands.find`, i.e. FIRST match in array order, and the server returns native before skills (SessionManager.ts:16044) — so if the shadow-skip is removed without also filtering the native list, the menu shows two `/review` rows and typing `/review` still runs the command file. Resolution side: RPC packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts:323 accepts any id string from the renderer. Tests that pin current behaviour: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.test.ts:172-178 and packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/custom-slash-command-boundary.test.ts:516-614; packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/adjacent-backend-frozen-contract.test.ts:662 only stubs `resolveCustomSlashCommand` and does not pin precedence. No persistence boundary: nothing about the collision is written to disk, and neither `CustomSlashCommand` nor `ResolvedCustomSlashCommand` (packages/shared/src/slash-commands/common.ts:6-12, custom-commands.ts:50-59) changes shape. It does cross the renderer↔server RPC as DATA — the id a user's `/review` submits changes from `custom:review` to `custom:skill:review` — and it crosses the packages/shared ↔ packages/server-core boundary, so both packages' tests must run.
userImpact: Concrete and reachable: install or author a skill whose name matches an existing command file — `review`, `deploy`, `fix-issue`, exactly the generic names Claude's own docs use as examples — and the skill vanishes from the `/` menu. The user sees one `/review`, picks it, and gets the `commands/review.md` prompt instead of the skill; there is no second, namespaced `/review` row to reach the skill from, because the skill is dropped before it is pushed (custom-commands.ts:444 vs :447). The only remaining routes are model auto-invocation or hand-typing the `[skill:review]` marker, neither of which is discoverable from the composer. Same effect from a workflow recipe of that name. A user following Claude's documentation ('shadow the command with a skill of the same name') gets the opposite of what the page promises, silently — no diagnostic is logged for the drop.
